pages.lesson:
LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: IMAGINATIVE COMPOSITION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Writing 3.3 Guided writing (2 sessions) • Vocabulary building- animals and birds
Topic 3.5: Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition, part of Writing 3.3 Guided writing (2 sessions) • Vocabulary building- animals and birds in Grade 9 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: How can one develop a creative story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. construct sentences using acquired vocabulary for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. create a short personal and imaginative composition for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate different Arabic writing styles.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. construct sentences using acquired vocabulary for comprehension,

   Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. create a short personal and imaginative composition for comprehension,

   Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate different Arabic writing styles.

   Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly to construct sentences using vocabulary related to making plans and appointments,

2. collaborate with peers in rearranging jumbled-up words to make meaningful sentences,

3. use a substitution table to form meaningful sentences and share with peers,

4. create a personal imaginative composition using the vocabulary identified in the theme,

5. share their best-written composition in the class gallery,

6. conduct interclass writing contests to write essays and imaginative compositions.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to construct sentences using vocabulary related to making plans and appointments,
2. collaborate with peers in rearranging jumbled-up words to make meaningful sentences,
3. use a substitution table to form meaningful sentences and share with peers,
4. create a personal imaginative composition using the vocabulary identified in the theme,
5. share their best-written composition in the class gallery,
6. conduct interclass writing contests to write essays and imaginative compositions.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and Problem-solving: This is promoted as the learner explores views when using a substitution table to

form meaningful sentences in groups.

● Communication and Collaboration: This is promoted as the learner engages actively to conduct an interclass writing

contest to write essays and imaginative compositions.

Values:
Love: This is promoted as the learner portrays a caring attitude to others when sharing their best-written composition in the

class gallery.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Economic resources: The learner will appreciate and recognise the importance of making plans as they write compositions on

the theme and interact with related vocabulary.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of activities done for fun and enjoyment to their learning of creative and constructive tasks

in Creative Arts and Sports.
